outcome: No core model containing all large cardinals has been constructed or shown not to exist; the closest bearing result (Aguilera, Bagaria & Lücke, 2024-2025) is a conditional theorem about the technical Weak HOD/Weak Ultimate-L Conjectures, not a resolution of the general 'ultimate core model' problem, and it does not settle whether such a model exists.

disputes.summary: A MathOverflow thread (referencing the Aguilera-Bagaria-Lücke papers, labeled [ABL24]/[ABGL25] there) asks open questions about whether exacting cardinals are compatible with V = Ultimate-L at all, and what the correct large-cardinal hierarchy looks like if the HOD Conjecture holds instead. This shows the community treats the bearing of these papers on Ultimate-L/the core-model program as still unsettled and under active discussion, not as a closed matter.

summary: The Wikipedia bullet is the general, informal problem of constructing a single canonical inner model ('the ultimate core model') that contains all large cardinals present in V — Woodin's broad core-model-theory program, of which the Ultimate-L Conjecture is one concrete formalization. Nothing in the window (26 Jan 2024 to today) constructs such a model, proves it cannot exist, or otherwise settles the general problem; the article on Core model (fetched today) still describes this as an open, active research area and cites nothing newer than 2013. The one line of work that plausibly bears on it is a pair of papers by Juan P. Aguilera, Joan Bagaria and Philipp Lücke: 'Large cardinals, structural reflection, and the HOD Conjecture' (arXiv:2411.11568, first submitted 18 Nov 2024, latest v4 16 Sep 2025) and the companion 'Large cardinals beyond HOD' (arXiv:2509.10254, submitted 12 Sep 2025). These introduce 'exacting' and 'ultraexacting' cardinals and prove (Theorem B of 2411.11568, read directly from the arXiv HTML): 'Suppose that the theory ZFC is consistent with the assumption that there is an extendible cardinal below an exacting cardinal. Then, the Weak HOD Conjecture and the Weak Ultimate-L Conjecture are false.' This is a conditional (relative-consistency) result about the Weak HOD and Weak Ultimate-L Conjectures specifically — named, narrower conjectures in the Ultimate-L program — not an unconditional theorem, and not a statement about the Wikipedia bullet's own general question of whether an ultimate core model exists. Reading these Weak conjectures' refutation as bearing on the general problem stated in this bullet would be treating a related, more specific conjecture as if it were the stated question; per §3.1 that makes it a related-problem result rather than a case of this problem, so it does not move the status here. No search turned up any AI system (LLM, automated theorem prover, or otherwise) anywhere in this line of work: neither paper's text (fetched directly) mentions AI, GPT, Claude, Copilot, Lean, or any proof assistant, and a further search for 'exacting cardinal'/'ultraexacting' combined with AI terms returned nothing connecting them. Broader searches for AI-assisted work on the Ultimate-L program or core models generally (e.g. work on LLMs as provers/verifiers, autoformalization surveys) found generic AI-mathematics research unrelated to this specific problem. I am satisfied nothing has happened to the general 'ultimate core model' problem itself in this window, and that no AI was involved in the one adjacent development that exists.
competing_reading: A looser reading could count the Aguilera-Bagaria-Lücke result as `progress` on this bullet on the theory that the Ultimate-L Conjecture is the leading candidate formalization of 'the ultimate core model' and that conditionally refuting the Weak Ultimate-L Conjecture (and, if the exacting-cardinal consistency holds, the full Ultimate-L Conjecture and HOD Conjecture too) narrows the space of plausible ultimate-core-model programs. Under that reading the status would be `progress` with `ai_role` `none` and `resolution_direction` `null` (since the theorem itself is conditional, no direction is settled outright). I judged this a related-problem case rather than a case of the stated problem because (a) the result is explicitly conditional on the unresolved consistency of exacting cardinals with an extendible cardinal below them, so nothing is unconditionally refuted; (b) it targets the Weak versions of two named conjectures, not the general existence question Wikipedia poses; and (c) the MathOverflow discussion shows experts treat the relationship between exacting cardinals and Ultimate-L as an open question rather than a settled blow to the program.
what_would_settle_it: Either (a) an unconditional proof (or disproof) that an ultimate core model containing all large cardinals exists, (b) an unconditional (non-relative-consistency) refutation of the full Ultimate-L Conjecture itself, which would be a much stronger and squarely on-topic result, or (c) an authoritative expert account (e.g. from Woodin, Aguilera, Bagaria, or Lüücke) explicitly stating that their exacting-cardinal results settle, or are widely regarded by the field as settling, the general core-model existence question rather than only the named Weak conjectures.
